title: Rebuild the status page on the new design
summary: The status page gets the new look — a map rail down the left, a next-action band up top, and cards that show what each work item is actually contracted to do. It widens the data feed first so the page has something to show, hands the reader control of when the page refreshes, fixes a state the design forgot, and rewrites the page's own tests so a restyle can never quietly delete them.
motivation: The page shows what git knows but almost nothing of what the binder says, and it refreshes on a fixed timer the reader cannot see or stop.

included: skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py — the state feed join, the CSS, the Vue template and app, the refresh model, and the self-test
skills/karta-status/assets/fonts/ — the three vendored font families
the generated Codex mirrors under .agents/skills/ and plugins/karta/
excluded: the stack: Vue 3 stays vendored, the server stays Python stdlib http.server, the feed stays JSON — no htmx, no build step, no single-file components, no TypeScript, no second front-end library
the design's 'Example · not a live binder' marker — mock scaffolding, not a feature
any new git call; every field the redesign needs is already gathered or is string formatting over it
the engine (karta_next.py) — this binder does not change how state is derived
the derivation performance work, which lands in its predecessor binder
prose docs beyond the operator how-to; doc-gardner corrects the rest after delivery

design_facts.stack: Python stdlib http.server + vendored Vue 3 SPA, shipped as a Claude Code / Codex plugin skill

token_manifest.mechanism: CSS custom properties. The design switches themes on a data-theme attribute alone; the shipped page must keep its wider cascade — bare :root, a prefers-color-scheme override, and both data-theme selectors — so the system default and the ?theme=light|dark forced override both keep working.

type_roles.Newsreader: wordmark 21/500, binder headline 40/400, item titles 20, rail card titles 17, hero band 24, wave numerals 25 with tabular-nums
type_roles.IBM Plex Mono: every label, eyebrow, chip, count, path, ref and inline command

work_items.title: Carry the missing binder fields through to the page
work_items.summary: Pass each work item's contract, files, size, serialization and full assertion list — plus an opt-out's reason and the binder's stack packs — into the live feed, without asking git for anything new.

contract.exposes: each item in /state.json gains contract, touches, estimate, serialize, shared_resources, the full assertions array, and oracle_reason; each binder row gains sme
contract.assertions_change: today only assertions[0] survives as `assert`; the whole array is now carried. The existing single-value key stays as the first assertion so nothing downstream breaks mid-binder
contract.opt_out_change: today an opt-out oracle is flattened to the type string 'opt-out' and its reason discarded; the reason is now carried alongside
contract.cost: pure pass-through from already-loaded binder JSON — zero additional git calls, which is what the gap analysis in docs/specs/2026-08-15-watch-performance-baseline.md concluded the redesign needs
contract.safety: every added value is engine-derived and must reach the browser through _inert_json like the rest of the state; none of it may be bound with v-html
contract.absence: a field the binder does not carry is emitted as null, never as an empty string, so the page can tell 'no contract' from 'a blank contract'
contract.verification_honesty: this gate is pure Python with no browser, no Vue runtime and no network. Where an assertion here reads as a claim about what a reader sees — that something renders, that a token resolves, that an animation settles, that a font falls back — it is verified against the rendered source and the resolved token tables, not against a painted page. The build report states which guarantees are proven by direct call, which by source inspection, and which need the human browser checklist the closing sweep produces.

signals: contract — /state.json is a published wire surface; every reader of the feed sees a wider shape, and this is the one item the whole binder depends on
blast-radius — serve_status.py is edited by every item in this binder
not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated

assertions: an item declaring contract, touches, estimate, serialize and shared_resources renders all five in the feed with the binder's own values
an oracle with three assertions renders all three, in order, not just the first
an opt-out oracle renders both its type and its recorded reason
the binder row carries its sme list
an item that declares none of these renders each as null, and the page still renders
the derivation issues no more git calls than before this change
every added value reaches the page through _inert_json: a binder whose contract or touches contain script markup renders inert, and no state-derived string is bound with v-html

the inertness check uses several vectors, not just a script tag — an img with an error handler, an svg with a load handler, a mixed-case script tag, and a javascript: URL — since escaping that stops one of these can miss the others
the regenerated Codex mirrors of serve_status.py are byte-identical to the canonical file

work_items.title: Rewrite the page's own tests so a restyle cannot silently delete them
work_items.summary: Give the markup stable test hooks and convert the checks that match exact CSS text and literal markup into checks on structure, so the redesign can change how things look without coverage quietly disappearing.

contract.exposes: a stable data-kw-* attribute hook grammar on every region and card the tests care about, borrowed from the design source's own attribute idiom, plus a migrated self-test whose rendered-output checks assert structure — an attribute, an element relationship, a resolved token name — never an exact CSS declaration or a literal markup string
contract.consumes: the widened feed, so the migrated checks cover the new fields too
contract.scope_of_migration: the exact-string block currently around serve_status.py:3604-3733 — page title, shell hooks, the home link text, the switcher, the delivered-binder colour rules, the reduced-motion rule, aria-expanded and aria-pressed markup, and the chip vocabulary
contract.no_visual_change: this item adds hooks and rewrites assertions only; the page must look the same before and after
contract.ordering_rationale: this lands second, immediately after the feed widening and before any restyle. Every later item breaks the existing exact-string assertions, so migrating last would leave every restyle item with a red oracle and nothing to merge on. Migrating first gives the later items a green, meaningful gate. This is also the enforced form of house rule hvue.4
contract.registry_not_a_name_list: the anti-coverage-loss guard is a CODE-SIDE REGISTRY mapping each behaviour name to the callable that checks it — not a count and not a list of strings. A bare count or name list is defeatable three ways, and the registry closes all three: PADDING (adding trivial checks to satisfy 'at least as many') fails because the registry is keyed on behaviour, so a new check does not substitute for a missing one; WEAKENING (rewriting an equality check into a substring check that still counts) fails because each entry names the specific property asserted, and the migrated check must still distinguish a correct render from a deliberately broken one; RENAMING (renaming a hook so the name list still matches while coverage drifts) fails because the registry binds a behaviour to a callable, and a renamed hook makes that callable fail rather than silently match a stale name
contract.negative_control: each migrated check must be demonstrated to FAIL against a deliberately broken render. A check never observed failing is not known to work, and a substring check that matches everything would otherwise pass the migration unnoticed
contract.preserved_behaviour_inventory: every one of these keeps a check: routes / and /state.json and /assets/<f>, hub / and /r/<slug>/ and /r/<slug>/state.json and /identity; hub token gating via constant-time comparison, Host pinning to 127.0.0.1:<port> and localhost:<port>, asset-directory confinement, _inert_json escaping; theme persistence under karta-theme, the show-delivered toggle under karta-show-delivered, the poll loop and its interval, the live/paused debounce after two consecutive failures, file:// snapshot mode with no polling, expand and collapse state, the empty state with its mascot, the degraded state, hub landing cards, the 'also watching:' switcher, and the ?theme=light|dark forced override
contract.external_anchor: the behaviours that must never disappear are anchored OUTSIDE serve_status.py — the one file every item edits — where validate_plugin.py can compare against them, and no LATER item touches it — this item creates the anchor and wires the comparison, which is why both files are in its touches. The comparison is a FLOOR, not equality: every anchored behaviour must be present in the registry, and extra registered behaviours are fine. Equality would be self-defeating, because later items each introduce new behaviours and a frozen anchor compared by equality would make every one of them a failure. A floor closes the hole that matters — deleting a registry entry together with its expected key in one edit now fails, because the anchor still names it and the anchor is not in the file being edited — while leaving addition open.
contract.additions_are_the_adding_item_s_job: each later item registers the behaviours it introduces and asserts its own new data-kw-* hooks are registered. Enforcement stays with the item that creates the region rather than being deferred to a sweep at the end, so an unhooked region fails where it is introduced instead of eleven items later.
contract.anchor_artifact: the anchor is a committed file this item CREATES — a plain list of the behaviour names that must never disappear — read by validate_plugin.py. Naming it as living 'outside serve_status.py' without an item creating it would leave the floor check comparing against nothing and passing vacuously, which is the failure mode the anchor exists to prevent. It is in this item's touches, and no later item edits it.
contract.registry_entries_have_a_kind: registry entries are of TWO kinds and the distinction is structural, not cosmetic. A RENDERED entry guards something visible and names the data-kw-* hook it binds to. A BEHAVIOUR entry guards something with no markup at all — token gating, the Host pin, asset confinement, inert-JSON escaping, the poll interval — and names the check that exercises it instead. Without the split, any audit demanding that every entry resolve to a hook is unsatisfiable, because roughly a third of the inventory has no hook and never will; the audit would then be permanently red or quietly weakened, which is the very failure the registry exists to prevent.
contract.verification_honesty: this gate is pure Python with no browser, no Vue runtime and no network. Where an assertion here reads as a claim about what a reader sees — that something renders, that a token resolves, that an animation settles, that a font falls back — it is verified against the rendered source and the resolved token tables, not against a painted page. The build report states which guarantees are proven by direct call, which by source inspection, and which need the human browser checklist the closing sweep produces.

signals: destructive — this item rewrites the suite that guards the whole page; the failure mode is deleting coverage rather than migrating it, and no other check would notice
contract — the data-kw-* hook grammar becomes a cross-item invariant every later item in this binder must honour
blast-radius — serve_status.py is edited by every item in this binder
not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated

assertions: the coverage registry maps every entry in this item's preserved-behaviour inventory to a callable, and the suite fails if any entry maps to nothing — so a later item cannot drop a behaviour by deleting its check

every behaviour named in the anchor outside serve_status.py is present in the registry — deleting a registry entry and its expected key in one edit fails, because the anchor is not in the file being edited. Extra registered behaviours pass, so a later item can add its own
every registered check is demonstrated to FAIL against a deliberately broken render of the behaviour it guards, so a check that matches everything cannot survive the migration
adding an unrelated trivial check does not satisfy a missing registry entry, proving the guard counts behaviours rather than checks
renaming a hook that a registered check depends on makes that check fail rather than silently pass, proving the registry binds to behaviour rather than to a stale name
no rendered-output assertion compares against an exact CSS declaration or a literal markup fragment; each asserts an attribute, an element relationship, or a resolved token name
the delivered-binder treatment is asserted as 'the delivered binder's node carries the delivered hook and resolves to the green token', not as a CSS rule string
the reduced-motion behaviour is asserted as 'the status indicator still animates under reduced motion using the karta-breathe keyframe', not as a literal rule
aria-expanded on the binder and work-item disclosures, and aria-pressed on the show-delivered toggle, are asserted as attributes on the right elements
the rendered page is byte-comparable to the pre-migration page apart from the added hook attributes, proving no visual change rode along

the harness that builds each negative control confirms its mutation actually changed the rendered bytes before running the check, so a mutation that silently stopped mutating cannot let every control pass vacuously
the regenerated Codex mirrors of serve_status.py are byte-identical to the canonical file
the anchor file exists, is committed, is non-empty, and validate_plugin.py fails when it is emptied — so the floor cannot pass by comparing against nothing

every registry entry declares its kind, rendered or behaviour; a rendered entry names an existing data-kw-* hook and a behaviour entry names the check that exercises it, and an entry with neither fails

work_items.title: Ship the page's three typefaces from the plugin itself
work_items.summary: Subset and vendor Newsreader, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono so the page gets the design's typography without ever reaching a font CDN.

contract.exposes: EIGHT subset woff2 files under skills/karta-status/assets/fonts/ served through the existing same-origin /assets/<f> route, declared with @font-face and font-display: swap — Newsreader 400 and 500 (2), IBM Plex Sans 400, 500 and 600 (3), IBM Plex Mono 400, 500 and 600 (3). Eight, not nine: the count and the list must agree, and the oracle asserts the number it can actually enumerate
contract.why: the design loads all three from Google Fonts; karta forbids CDN references, so they are served same-origin instead
contract.subsetting_by_writing_system_not_by_curr: the subset is cut to a FIXED writing-system range — Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, and General Punctuation — and NOT to 'the characters the page currently renders'. Two reasons, both fatal to the naive approach. First, this item lands early in the chain and later items introduce copy that does not exist yet, so a subset cut now would be missing glyphs by the end of the binder. Second, the page renders binder-authored content — titles, summaries, contract text, file paths — which is unbounded and cannot be enumerated at all. Content outside the range degrades to the system fallback, which is an accepted and documented consequence rather than a defect
contract.payload_budget: the eight files together stay under 400 KB. A subset with no stated bound is how a plugin quietly gains megabytes; the number is checkable in pure Python, so it is enforced rather than hoped for
contract.licensing: each family ships its licence file alongside the fonts, in every mirror. All three are Open Font Licence families, and a redistributed font without its licence is a licensing defect, not a tidiness one
contract.fallback: each family keeps a system-font fallback in its stack, so a missing or blocked font file degrades to readable text rather than an unstyled page
contract.constraint: these are font files, not a front-end library — Vue remains the only vendored runtime, per house rule hvue.2
contract.coverage_is_manifest_declared_not_parsed: reading a woff2 cmap table to prove glyph coverage needs a font library, and this gate is stdlib Python with zero dependencies — so an assertion that each face 'covers Basic Latin' would either be faked or quietly skipped. Coverage is instead a guarantee of the subsetting step, recorded in a manifest committed beside the fonts: per face, its family, weight, file, size, sha256 and the unicode-range it was cut to. The gate checks what it honestly can — that the manifest, the files on disk and the @font-face declarations agree with each other.
contract.verification_honesty: this gate is pure Python with no browser, no Vue runtime and no network. Where an assertion here reads as a claim about what a reader sees — that something renders, that a token resolves, that an animation settles, that a font falls back — it is verified against the rendered source and the resolved token tables, not against a painted page. The build report states which guarantees are proven by direct call, which by source inspection, and which need the human browser checklist the closing sweep produces.

the font manifest, the files on disk and the @font-face declarations agree: every manifest entry has a file whose size and sha256 match, every file is declared, and every declaration's unicode-range matches its manifest entry
the eight font files together are under 400 KB
each family ships a licence file, present and byte-identical in the canonical tree and both Codex mirrors

the rendered page loads nothing over http:// or https:// — checked against fetchable contexts (src, href, url(), @import), so an inline SVG namespace declaration does not false-fail, so nothing leaks to a CDN

work_items.title: Put the reader in charge of when the page refreshes
work_items.summary: Slow the automatic refresh to every thirty seconds, show a countdown to the next one, add a button that refreshes on demand, and let the reader switch automatic refreshing off entirely.

component_map.design: not in the design source
component_map.implementation: NEW — a refresh cluster in the header holding the countdown, the manual refresh button, and the automatic-refresh toggle. The design does not draw this; it is designed to sit in the header alongside the theme toggle and follow the same pill treatment

icon_map.use: the automatic-refresh toggle, matching the show-delivered toggle's idiom

contract.interval: the automatic refresh moves from 2.6 seconds to 30 seconds. On a twenty-binder repo that takes one open tab from 23.6% of a core to 2.0% before any other change lands — see docs/specs/2026-08-15-watch-performance-baseline.md
contract.three_states: automatic ON polls every 30 seconds and shows a countdown to the next refresh; automatic OFF polls not at all and shows the AGE of the data in place of the countdown, so staleness stays visible; manual refresh is available in both states, fetches exactly once, and when automatic is on it resets the countdown
contract.off_means_off: turning automatic refresh off must genuinely STOP the requests — the timer is cleared and no fetch is issued. Hiding the countdown while continuing to poll is a defect, not a cosmetic shortcut: each poll is real git work, up to 613 ms of it on a twenty-binder repo, which is the entire reason the control exists
contract.countdown_is_local: the countdown is a local timer over a known interval and must not itself cost a network request
contract.persistence: the automatic-on-or-off choice persists across reloads under the localStorage key `karta-auto-refresh`, following the existing pattern set by karta-theme and karta-show-delivered. The key is NAMED here rather than left to build time: an unnamed key is how two spellings end up in the same file and the setting silently stops persisting
contract.vocabulary: 'automatic refresh off' is a deliberate reader choice and must never be worded or styled as the existing 'feed paused' state, which means the feed failed twice in a row. The two are separate conditions and the page must not conflate a choice with a fault
contract.shape: an ordinary Options API addition to the existing app root — added state, a computed countdown, and methods. The timer and any listener added at mount are torn down in beforeUnmount alongside the existing poll timer, per house rule hvue.1 and the vue.6 teardown rule
contract.decision_logic: the refresh branching lands as a PURE PYTHON FUNCTION with a named signature — refresh_decision(mode: str, visible: bool, elapsed_ms: int, interval_ms: int, manual: bool) -> str returning one of 'skip', 'poll', 'poll-now' — mirrored verbatim into the rendered client with the MIRROR comment, exactly as _feed_transition and poll_decision already are. In manual-only mode the function returns 'skip' for every elapsed time and 'poll-now' only for a manual trigger; that is the enforceable form of off-means-off
contract.what_the_gate_can_and_cannot_see: the acceptance check is a Python self-test with no browser, no Vue runtime, no localStorage and no network. It verifies the pure decision function by direct call, and static properties of the RENDERED JS SOURCE — that a storage key is read and written, that timers and listeners have matching teardown, that the countdown derives from local state rather than a fetch. It CANNOT observe that a real browser issued no request, and no assertion here may be written as though it could. The behavioural guarantee is stated in the build report as verified by the decision function plus source inspection, not end to end
contract.preserved: file:// snapshot mode still never polls in either state; the two-consecutive-failure live/paused debounce is unchanged; the visibility backoff landed by the predecessor binder still applies when automatic refresh is on
contract.no_bypass_fetch: off-means-off is only real if the decision function gates EVERY request initiator, not a lexical 'poll path'. The predecessor binder's conditional revalidation is itself a fetch, and a visibility, focus or online handler can start one too — any of which would keep touching git while the page claims refresh is off. The rendered client must therefore have exactly one poll timer, distinct from the countdown ticker, and every fetch call site other than the initial load must sit behind a refresh_decision result.
contract.baseline_reset_lives_in_the_caller: a pure function returning a string cannot reset anything; the elapsed baseline is caller state. The caller resets it when the decision returns poll-now, and that wiring is checked at the source level rather than asserted of the function.
contract.edge_cases: automatic refresh is ON by default on a first visit; a browser where storage is unavailable falls back to that default rather than failing; and a manual refresh while one is already in flight does not start a second.
contract.verification_honesty: assertions here about what a BROWSER does — a request not issued, a listener torn down, storage persisting across a reload, a layout reflowing at a breakpoint, an animation resolving to a static state, a clipboard call degrading — are verified at the source level, not end to end. The gate has no browser. The build report states which guarantees are proven by direct call, which by source inspection, and which are not machine-verifiable at all and need a human to look.
contract.visibility_lives_inside_the_decision: the visible parameter is gated INSIDE refresh_decision, not before the call. If visibility were checked by the caller instead, the parameter would be dead and the claim that every fetch sits behind a refresh_decision result would be false — the visibility gate would be a second, separate, untested path. Inside the function it is covered by the same direct-call assertions as everything else. The predecessor binder's poll_decision handled visibility for the old loop; this function subsumes that and the predecessor's backoff must not survive as a parallel check.
contract.manual_overrides_hidden: a manual refresh works on a hidden tab. Someone who clicks refresh has asked for it, and honouring a deliberate action does not reintroduce background polling.
contract.mirror_check_limits: one honest limit: a pure-Python gate cannot execute or semantically diff JavaScript, so 'the mirror is logically identical' is not a claim it can make. contract.ordering_rationale: this lands BEFORE the panel that counts these states. The other way round leaves a commit where the counts row tallies six states while only five can render, so the totals provably cannot add up and the tree is knowingly incoherent between two items.
contract.verification_honesty: this gate is pure Python with no browser, no Vue runtime and no network. Where an assertion here reads as a claim about what a reader sees — that something renders, that a token resolves, that an animation settles, that a font falls back — it is verified against the rendered source and the resolved token tables, not against a painted page. The build report states which guarantees are proven by direct call, which by source inspection, and which need the human browser checklist the closing sweep produces.
contract.built_treatment: the design source has no card for this state, but it does not need a new colour — it already has a grammar for this. Border weight says how much attention a card wants; fill says which state it is in. Passed is a green FILL with a neutral border. Built is the same green as a BORDER, THIN — matching passed and ready, not the 2px that running and halted use, because an item awaiting merge is calm — with NO green fill. Same hue, inverted weight. No token is added: a new hue would be a seventh in a palette of six related warm tones plus one steel, and would read as foreign beside them.
contract.weight_alone_is_not_the_whole_signal: fill-versus-outline is a weight difference, not a hue difference, so it survives colour-blindness and greyscale — but it is deliberately not the only cue. The git-merge glyph and the state word carry the distinction independently. A reader who cannot resolve a pale tint against a thin border still reads the icon and the label. Whether the pair actually separates at a scan is a perceptual question the gate cannot answer, so it goes on the closing sweep's human checklist rather than being asserted.
contract.metadata_exposes_both_roles: the state metadata table carries THREE named fields per state: the border token, the fill token, and the border weight as a named role — calm or urgent — not a pixel value. Without the third field the weight assertion has no structural source and collapses into matching an exact CSS string, which the self-test migration forbids. With it, calm covers passed, ready and built; urgent covers running and halted; and waiting is calm with a dashed edge.

It also includes one comparison the gate cannot make: a passed card and a built card side by side, in both themes, confirming they separate at a scan rather than only under inspection. signals: contract — this is the last gate before the redesign is considered complete, and it is the only item that checks the states no other item owns
blast-radius — serve_status.py is edited by every item in this binder
not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated

assertions: the empty state renders on the new palette and type roles, with its mascot, and resolves only defined tokens
the degraded state renders on the new palette and resolves only defined tokens

the file:// snapshot renders the whole page with no server: it registers no timer, and with the vendored font routes unavailable every font stack still resolves to a system fallback so the text stays readable
the ?theme=light and ?theme=dark forced renders each produce their palette and contain the rail, the band and the item-card hooks
the 404 page renders on the new tokens

every data-kw-* hook in the rendered page has a RENDERED registry entry, and every rendered entry resolves to a hook that exists. Behaviour entries — token gating, the Host pin, confinement, escaping, the poll interval — are audited by their checks running, since they have no markup to resolve to
each of the five keyframes has a stated behaviour under a reduced-motion preference, and none of them is left animating unconditionally

the rendered page loads nothing over http:// or https:// — checked against fetchable contexts (src, href, url(), @import), so an inline SVG namespace declaration does not false-fail in any of these states
the regenerated Codex mirrors of serve_status.py are byte-identical to the canonical file
every data-kw-* hook this item introduces is present in the coverage registry, so a missing registration fails here and names this item rather than surfacing later as a sweep failure
the item produces the named human browser checklist, and it covers every guarantee the build reports marked as not machine-verifiable — so the unverifiable set is enumerated rather than forgotten
